extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (appellants, attorneys, agents) involved in appeals and examiner's answers
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for appeal practice before the USPTO Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, focusing on appeal conferences, reply briefs, examiner's answer content/format, and handling of reopenings/new grounds. Useful for examiners drafting answers and practitioners preparing or replying to appeal briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief timing and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a reply brief to an examiner’s answer or a supplemental examiner’s answer within two months from the date of such examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.136(b) for extensions of time for filing a reply brief in a patent application and §1.550(c) for extensions of time in a reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner action on reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner must either acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief or withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner’s answer is not permitted unless the application has been remanded by the Board for such purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options when prosecution is reopened to avoid abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where prosecution is reopened after an appeal or reply brief has been filed, appellant must either (i) file a reply under §1.111 if the Office action is not final, or under §1.113 if the Office action is final; or (ii) request reinstatement of the appeal accompanied by a supplemental appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting reinstatement with a supplemental appeal brief, no new amendments, affidavits (§§1.130, 1.131 or 1.132) or other evidence are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases in which an acceptable brief (MPEP §1206) has been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner charged with preparing the examiner’s answer concludes the appeal should not go forward and the SPE approves, then no appeal conference is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference participants and recordation
rubrics_metrics.description: The participants of the appeal conference should include (1) the examiner charged with preparation of the examiner’s answer, (2) a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and (3) another examiner (a conferee) with sufficient experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider dropping cumulative art rejections and eliminating technical rejections of doubtful value. On the examiner’s answer, below the primary examiner’s signature, include 'Conferees:' followed by typed/printed names of the other two participants; these participants must place their initials next to their name to make the record clear that an appeal conference has been held.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board review for appeal conference notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the appeal case, the Board should review the application prior to assigning an appeal number to determine whether an appeal conference has been held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner’s answer lacks indication that an appeal conference has been held (names and initials of conferees), the Board should return the application to the appropriate TC Director for corrective action (not considered a remand). Applies to answers received on or after Nov 1, 2000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure approved amendments are physically entered before answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Before preparing the answer, the examiner should make certain that all amendments approved for entry have in fact been physically entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clerk of the Board will return to the TC any application in which approved amendments have not been entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should furnish the appellant with a written statement in answer to the appellant’s brief within 2 months after the receipt of the brief by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The answer should contain a response to the allegations or arguments in the brief and should call attention to any errors in appellant’s copy of the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling affidavits/declarations/exhibits filed with/after notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should treat affidavits, declarations, or exhibits filed with or after the notice of appeal in accordance with 37 CFR 1.195.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an affidavit/declaration/exhibit was refused entry under 37 CFR 1.195, the examiner should not comment on it in the examiner’s answer; likewise appellant should not rely on such refused evidence in an appeal brief. Challenges to non-entry should be by timely petition seeking supervisory review. Affidavits swearing behind a patent should be identified as being considered under 37 CFR 1.131 or 1.608(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference in examiner’s answer limited to single prior action
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may incorporate in the answer their statement of the grounds of rejection merely by reference to the final rejection (or a single other action on which it is based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only statements appearing in a single prior action may be incorporated by reference; an examiner’s answer should not refer to more than one prior action. If statements of grounds appear in other actions, they should be quoted in the answer with page/paragraph explicitly identified. Include necessary rebuttal of appellant’s arguments if final action does not adequately meet the arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluate and withdraw rejections not adhered to
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should reevaluate his/her position in light of the arguments presented in the brief and should expressly withdraw any rejections not adhered to, especially if the rejection was made in an action which is incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection not repeated and discussed in the answer may be taken by the Board as having been withdrawn (Ex parte Emm).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new ground of rejection in examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: A new ground of rejection is no longer permitted in an examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new ground of rejection is necessary, prosecution must be reopened and the examiner must obtain supervisory approval prior to reopening prosecution after an appeal. See MPEP §1208.01 and §1002.02(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: All correspondence with the Board must be on the record; unpublished decisions restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence with the Board, whether by the examiner or the appellant, must be on the record. No unpublished decisions unavailable to the general public by reason of 35 U.S.C. 122(a) can be cited by the examiner or the appellant, except when either has the right to cite an unpublished decision in an application having common ownership with the application on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: File handling: include soft copies/prints of references in file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: When files are forwarded, soft copies and prints of references therein should remain in the file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding examiner’s answer raising new interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer is believed to contain a new interpretation or application of existing patent law, the examiner’s answer, application file, and an explanatory memorandum should be forwarded to the TC Director for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved by the TC Director, forward to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy for final approval. See MPEP §1003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer must comply with 37 CFR 1.193 and include required headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs must comply with 37 CFR 1.192, and all examiner’s answers filed in response to such briefs must comply with the listed guidelines and include, under appropriate headings in the indicated order, specified items (Real Party in Interest; Related Appeals and Interferences; Status of Claims; Status of Amendments; Summary of Invention; Issues; Grouping of Claims; Claims Appealed; References of Record; Grounds of Rejection; Response to Argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner’s answer must include these items in the order indicated and under appropriate headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement acknowledging identification of the real party in financial interest or indicating that the party named in the caption of the brief is the real party in interest; if heading present but no identification, state it is presumed the caption party is the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the examiner will make this presumption, the Board has discretion to require an explicit statement on this item from appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related appeals and interferences statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement acknowledging appellant’s identification of related cases which will directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the decision in the pending appeal, or, if none identified under the heading, a statement that it is presumed there are none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may exercise discretion to require an explicit statement on this item from appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner agrees or disagrees with the statement of the status of claims contained in the brief and a correct statement of the status of all the claims pending or cancelled, if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner considers some or all of the finally rejected claims are allowable, see MPEP §1208.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with the statement of the status of amendments contained in the brief, and an explanation of any disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of invention statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with the summary of invention contained in the brief, an explanation of why the examiner disagrees, and a correct summary of the invention, if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues statement (including petitionable vs appealable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with the statement of the issues in the brief and an explanation of why the examiner disagrees, including identification of any issues which are petitionable rather than appealable and identification of any issues or grounds of rejection on appeal which the examiner no longer considers applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of claims statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with any statement in the brief that certain claims do not stand or fall together, and, if the examiner disagrees, an explanation as to why those claims are not separately patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief lacks the required statement or reasons that claims do not stand or fall together (37 CFR 1.192(c)(7)), notify appellant of non-compliance using appropriate form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appealed (copy accuracy) statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the copy of the appealed claims contained in the appendix to the brief is correct and, if not, include a correct copy of any incorrect claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors are significant, appellant should be required to submit a corrected brief and attach correct copies to the Examiner’s Answer; draw a diagonal line through the incorrect claim in appellant’s appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: References of record listing
rubrics_metrics.description: A listing of the references of record relied on, and, for nonpatent references, the relevant page or pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified formats for listing references (number, name, date) and provide examples as in MPEP §707.05(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection: general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each ground of rejection applicable to the appealed claims, an explanation of the ground of rejection, or reference to a final rejection or other single prior action for a clear exposition of the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain each ground or refer to a single prior Office action which sets forth the rejection and comply with the specific paragraph requirements for 35 U.S.C. 112, 102, 103, and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection – 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, the examiner’s answer (or single prior action) shall explain how the first paragraph of 35 U.S.C. 112 is not complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include, as appropriate, how the specification/drawings (i) do not describe the subject matter defined by each rejected claim, (ii) would not enable a person skilled in the art to make and use the subject matter without undue experimentation, and (iii) do not set forth the best mode contemplated by the appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection – 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, the examiner’s answer (or single prior action) shall explain how the claims do not particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which applicant regards as the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection – 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102, the examiner’s answer (or single prior action) shall explain why the rejected claims are anticipated or not patentable under 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out where all of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims are found in the prior art relied upon in the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of rejection – 35 U.S.C. 103 (obviousness) explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, the examiner’s answer (or single prior action) shall: (i) state the ground of rejection and point out where each of the specific limitations recited in the rejected claims is found in the prior art relied upon; (ii) identify any difference between the rejected claims and the prior art relied on; and (iii) explain how and why the claimed subject matter is rendered unpatentable over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rejection is based upon a combination of references, the answer (or single prior action) shall explain the rationale for making the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-by-feature comparison when claim-to-prior-art correspondence unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: For each rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 where there are questions as to how claim limitations correspond to features in the prior art, the examiner shall compare at least one of the rejected claims feature by feature with the prior art relied on in the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparison shall align the language of the claim side-by-side with a reference to the specific page, line number, drawing reference number, and quotation from the prior art, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to appellant’s arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of whether the examiner disagrees with each of the contentions of appellant in the brief with respect to the issues presented and an explanation of the reasons for disagreement with any such contention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any ground of rejection is not argued and replied to by appellant, the response shall point out each claim affected. If an issue raised by appellant was fully responded to under 'Grounds of Rejection', no additional response is required here; otherwise provide a full response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and cover sheet use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specified form paragraphs (e.g., ¶12.49 Examiner’s Answer Cover Sheet, ¶12.50 Heading For Examiner’s Answer, and follow-on form paragraphs) to structure the examiner’s answer and include required bracketed insertions (dates, claim numbers, paper numbers, names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Examiner Notes for proper insertion and sequencing of form paragraphs; e.g., form ¶12.50.01 Real Party in Interest, ¶12.51 Status of Claims, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to rejection in prior Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, an examiner may reference a prior Office action which fully sets forth a rejection, by identifying the claim(s), the statutory section (e.g., 35 U.S.C. [2]) and the prior Paper No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the Paper No. of the Office action in which the rejection is set forth in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s request to present oral arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant requested an oral hearing and the primary examiner intends to present an oral argument, the examiner may request the opportunity to present arguments at the oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the corresponding form paragraph only if an oral hearing has been requested by appellant; if examiner will attend as observer, note on file wrapper 'Examiner will attend (but not participate in) hearing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusion language when rejections sustained
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer should include a conclusion such as 'For the above reasons, it is believed that the rejections should be sustained.' and include signature, conferees, and correspondence address as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferees must place their initials next to their names; include correspondence address of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reopening prosecution when new ground required
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the time of preparing the answer the examiner decides a new ground of rejection should be applied, the examiner should reopen prosecution and obtain supervisory approval before reopening prosecution after an appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.193(a)(2) prohibits entry of a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer; see MPEP §1002.02(d) for supervisory approval requirements.
